fox-control-mornington-peninsula: How many foxes will you get in one night?
On a typical Peninsula hobby farm the first night takes two to five foxes. Numbers drop quickly after that, which is why the first visit sets up a follow-up a few weeks later.
Is shooting better than baiting for foxes?
On the Peninsula, yes. Most blocks are too close to neighbours, dogs and public land to lay 1080 or PAPP legally or safely. Shooting is target-specific and leaves nothing in the paddock.
When is the best time of year for fox control?
Late winter and spring during lambing and kidding, and again in autumn when the year's cubs disperse. For poultry losses, any time you are losing birds.
Will my dogs or horses be at risk?
No. We shoot only with a clear backstop, away from stock, and with thermal identification of every target. We work at a distance and animals settle quickly.
rabbit-control-mornington-peninsula: Can shooting alone get rid of rabbits?
Shooting knocks numbers down fast but does not finish a warren. We point you to the warrens we find so you can rip or fumigate them, which is what stops them coming back.
We use small-calibre rifles, worked at a distance from the house with a clear backstop. It is a controlled operation, not a loud one.
Yes. Rabbits ring-bark young vines, so spring sessions during establishment are our most common vineyard booking. We work after cellar-door hours.
deer-control-mornington-peninsula: Is it legal to shoot deer on my property?
Yes. Deer are unprotected on private land in Victoria and the landholder can authorise control. We hold a Game Licence and handle the authority paperwork.
Removed and disposed of, or dressed on site if you want the meat. Where a property has steady numbers we can often do regular visits free in exchange for harvesting.
Which deer are on the Peninsula?
Fallow are the most common, with red and hog deer around Arthurs Seat, Main Ridge, Red Hill and the Westernport bush.
feral-cat-control-mornington-peninsula: How do you know a cat is feral and not someone's pet?
No collar or ear tag, in bushland away from houses, and usually seen repeatedly on the same property. If there is any doubt the animal is left alone.
Do you trap as well as shoot?
Yes. On properties too close to neighbours for shooting alone we combine it with cage trapping.
Why control feral cats at all?
They are the main predator of bandicoots, hooded plover chicks and small reptiles on the Peninsula, and they raid aviaries and chook pens.
rat-control-mornington-peninsula: Rat baits kill owls, dogs and occasionally horses. On stables, chook pens and anywhere product is stored, shooting removes rats with nothing left behind.
Is shooting inside a shed safe?
We use air rifles and subsonic .22 from inside the building with a clear backstop, and we check the shed layout at the assessment first.
A two-hour evening visit usually removes the bulk of an infestation. We then advise on grain storage and sealing gaps.
vineyard-pest-control-mornington-peninsu: Can you work around cellar-door hours and events?
Yes. Sessions run after close, at dawn, or on days you nominate. We stay away from guest areas.
Do you leave anything in the vineyard?
No baits, no poisons and no carcasses. Deer are removed and warrens pointed out for your crew.
How often do vineyards book you?
Most run a monthly program from budburst to veraison, with extra visits if damage picks up.
horse-property-pest-control-mornington-p: Will the shooting spook my horses?
We work from the outside of the paddocks and never shoot across a paddock with stock in it, so horses usually settle quickly.
Can you do the rats in my feed room?
Yes. That is our most common horse-property booking: a two-hour evening visit with air rifle and subsonic .22, no baits.
We time fox nights to foaling season and work the dens near the foaling paddocks for a follow-up.
hobby-farm-pest-control-mornington-penin: My block is only five acres. Can you still shoot there?
Usually yes. Small blocks near neighbours need a Public Place Permit, which we hold, and the plan is set at a daytime assessment.
What does the first night cost?
The first night is a flat $50 callout. You see the count of what was taken before deciding on anything more.
What should I do before you arrive?
Lock dogs and cats inside, tell us where stock are, and leave outside lights as they normally are.
acreage-pest-control-mornington-peninsul: Is it legal to shoot on a lifestyle block near town?
Only with a Victoria Police Public Place Permit, which we hold. We also notify the local police station before each session.
Thermal optics mean no spotlights are used, and every session is planned around your property and timing to keep disturbance down.
How many visits do I need?
Most lifestyle blocks are one or two nights a year, timed to spring and to when the garden or poultry start suffering.
commercial-farm-pest-control-mornington-: Do you quote per visit or per program for a big property?
For working farms and multi-property operations we quote a per-hectare or per-program rate rather than per visit, so the cost matches the scale of the job.
Can you fit in around lambing and calving?
Yes. We build the program around your calendar and weight the work to the weeks either side of lambing and calving when losses peak.
Will you work in with our baiting and fencing contractors?
Yes. We coordinate with your existing baiting, warren-ripping and fencing so the whole control effort pulls together.
orchard-market-garden-pest-control-morni: Is anything left on the produce or in the soil?
No. Shooting is target-specific, with no baits, residues or food-safety concerns anywhere near crops or trees.
Can you work around picking and planting?
Yes. We work after hours and around harvest crews, and time visits to picking and planting schedules.
What damage are you controlling in an orchard?
Mainly rabbits ring-barking young trees and seedlings, deer browsing new growth, and foxes raiding poultry and digging soft ground.
pest-shooting-mornington-peninsula: Do you do termites, ants or general pest control?

No. We are licensed firearms shooters for feral and vermin animals — foxes, rabbits, deer, feral cats and rats. For termites, ants, cockroaches or spiders you want a chemical pest control company, which is a different trade. What we do is remove the actual animals with thermal-scoped shooting, with no baits or sprays.
Are you actually licensed to shoot on private property?

Yes. We hold a Victorian Category A/B firearms licence endorsed for vermin and feral animal control, a Game Licence for deer, public liability insurance, and a Victoria Police Public Place Permit for blocks close to houses and roads. The landholder authority paperwork is handled for you and the local police station is notified before each session.
Foxes, rabbits, deer (fallow, red and hog), feral cats and rats. If it is a feral or pest animal doing damage on the Peninsula, it is what we do; if it is an insect or a termite, it is not.
